title: Follow-ups become structural: complete_task gains follow_ups field
summary: Decision (2026-06-10): worker-discovered follow-ups must not live only as prose in complete_task summaries — nothing acts on prose. complete_task gains optional follow_ups: [{title, prompt, when?, disruptive?}]. Daemon turns each into a graph task with a context edge back to the parent; immediate ones drain via the existing loop; timed ones ride NATIVE scheduled tasks (write ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/{id}/SKILL.md — per B3 ride-the-substrate, no custom timer); disruptive ones (restarts/deploys/destructive) queue via the existing escalation gate (POST /guidance) instead of auto-firing. Rationale: execution (loop) and timing (native scheduler) already exist; the only gap was caveat→task. Caveat: daemon-written scheduled tasks have no stored tool approvals, so first unattended runs can stall on permission prompts.
